acceptance_checks: A parametrized bytes value run with Python -bb and --setup-show exits successfully without BytesWarning.
The bytes parameter is displayed using its safe bytes representation, such as b'Hello World', in both SETUP and TEARDOWN output.
Regression coverage exercises the bytes case under -bb.
Existing explicit list-ID and callable-ID setup-show tests continue to pass with unchanged displayed IDs.
No parameterization, fixture lifecycle, test-node ID, or non-setup-show behavior is changed.
confirmed_decisions: Apply saferepr to all raw fixture parameter values, not only bytes-like values.
Do not apply saferepr to explicit IDs supplied through an ID list or callable; preserve their existing rendering exactly.
Use saferepr's existing default size limit, allowing long raw parameter representations to be truncated.
Use the same safe raw-parameter representation for SETUP and TEARDOWN output.
Accept that raw string parameters may become quoted because raw parameters now use repr-style rendering.
Limit the change to --setup-show parameter rendering.
Acknowledge the bounded residual risk that other raw parameter types may have visibly different or truncated output under saferepr's default policy.
summary: For --setup-show only, render raw fixture parameter values with saferepr using its default size limit in both SETUP and TEARDOWN output. Explicit list-derived and callable-derived IDs must continue to render exactly as before. Raw strings may gain quotes; bytes must render as a bytes representation without raising BytesWarning under Python -bb; long values and objects with faulty repr implementations inherit saferepr's bounded, failure-safe behavior. Implementation scope is limited to setup-show parameter rendering and must not change parameterization, fixture lifecycle, test node IDs, or behavior when setup-show is disabled.
